verses.zh: 众海岛啊，当在我面前静默；众民当重新得力，都要近前来才可以说话，我们可以彼此辩论。
verses.en: “Listen to me in silence, you coastlands![NOTE:1] Let the nations find renewed strength!Let them approach and then speak;let us come together for debate.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “islands” (KJV, NIV, CEV); TEV “distant lands”; NLT “lands beyond the sea.”
The Hebrew term מִשְׁפָּט (mishpat) could be translated “judgment,” but here it seems to refer to the dispute or debate between the Lord and the nations.
verses.commentary:
41:1 Verse 1 is a literary technique used often in the OT (i.e. a court scene, cf. Isa. 1:18-20; 43:26;
50:8; Hosea 4; Micah 6). YHWH brings the nations, and in Isa. 41:21, their idols before His judgment seat.

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA
"coastlands"

TEV
"distant lands"

NJB, REB
"coasts and islands"

LXX
"O islands"

Peshitta
"O you islands"

The word (BDB 15) means "coast" or "region." Isaiah uses it often to refer to Gentile
nations in the Mediterranean area (cf. Isa. 11:11; 24:15; 41:1,5; 42:4,10,12; 49:1; 51:5; 59:18; 60:9; 66:19).

It is parallel to "peoples" (BDB 522, cf. Isa. 49:1). It seems that the nation of Edom is used
as a symbol for all "rebellious nations" (i.e. 34:5-17; 63:1-6; Jer. 49:7-22; Lam. 4:21-22; Ezek. 25:12-14;
35:1-15; Obadiah, Mal. 1:2-4). In Isaiah this term often stands for Gentile nations, like Philistia
and Phoenicia (cf. Isa. 23:2-6).

▣ "in silence" This is another term related to a court scene (cf. Hab. 2:20; Zech. 2:13). There
is nothing to say in light of YHWH's presence and power.

▣ "gain new strength" It is surprising (and uncertain in meaning) that the same VERB (BDB 322,
KB 321, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense)
used of God's people in Isa. 40:31, is now used for "the peoples" (i.e. Gentiles).

▣ "come forward" This VERB, "draw near" (BDB 620,
KB 670, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense)
can be used of priests approaching YHWH in sacrifice and worship, but here it is approaching the judge
for a defense (cf. Isa. 34:1; 48:16).

verses.zh: 谁从东方兴起一人，凭公义召他来到脚前呢？耶和华将列国交给他，使他管辖君王，把他们如灰尘交与他的刀，如风吹的碎秸交与他的弓。
verses.en: Who stirs up this one from the east?[NOTE:1] Who[NOTE:2] officially commissions him for service?[NOTE:3] He hands nations over to him[NOTE:4] and enables him to subdue[NOTE:5] kings.He makes them like dust with his sword,like windblown straw with his bow.[NOTE:6]
notes: The expression this one from the east refers to the Persian conqueror Cyrus, as later texts indicate (see 44:28-45:6; 46:11; 48:14-16).
The interrogative particle is understood by ellipsis.
Heb “[in] righteousness called him to his foot.”
Heb “he [the Lord] places before him [Cyrus] nations.”

The verb יַרְדְּ (yard) is an otherwise unattested Hiphil form from רָדָה (radah, “rule”). But the Hiphil makes no sense with “kings” as object; one must understand an ellipsis and supply “him” (Cyrus) as the object. The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has יוֹרִיד (yorid), which appears to be a Hiphil form from יָרַד (yarad, “go down”). Others suggest reading יָרֹד (yarod), a Qal form from רָדַד (radad, “beat down”).
The point is that they are powerless before Cyrus’ military power and scatter before him.
verses.commentary:
41:2

NASB, NRSV, JPSOA, LXX
"has aroused"

NKJV, REB
"has raised up"

TEV
"brought"

NJB
"has raised"

Peshitta
"has stirred up"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 734, KB 802, Hiphil
PERFECT),
which expresses YHWH's activity in history.

- used of YHWH Himself ‒ Deut. 32:11; Isa. 42:13; 51:5

- used of Assyria ‒ 1 Chr. 5:26

- used of Neo-Babylon's enemies ‒ Jer. 50:9; 51:1

- used of Medo-Persia ‒ Ezra 1:1; Isa. 13:17; 41:25; 45:13; Dan. 11:2

- other nations

- Philistia ‒ 2 Chr. 21:16

- against Judah ‒ Ezek. 23:22

for Judah ‒ Haggai 1:14

▣ "one from the east" This refers to Cyrus II (cf. "one from the north," Isa. 41:25). He is
mentioned specifically by name in Isa. 44:28; 45:1. Cyrus II, known as Cyrus the Great

- became King of Anshan in 558 B.C.

- gained control of Media in 550 B.C.

- controlled Lydia in 546 B.C.

- controlled Neo-Babylon in 539 B.C.

- issued a decree in 538 B.C. that all the deported people groups
exiled by Assyria and Babylon could go home, including the Jews

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF PERSIA

▣ "Whom He calls in righteousness" The JPSOA translates this by uniting the thoughts of lines
1 and 2, "who has roused a victor (BDB 841) from the east."

The Jewish Study Bible (864) mentions that the Targums translate this so as to refer to
Abraham whom YHWH called from Ur of the Chaldees (i.e. Gen. 15:6, where the same root, BDB 842, is used of Abraham).
If so, then the military part of Isa. 41:2 would refer to Genesis 14, Abraham's defeat of the kings.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "to His feet" It must be remembered that the Ark of the Covenant was viewed as the footstool
for YHWH's feet (i.e. 1 Chr. 28:2; Ps. 132:7; Isa. 66:1) and, thereby, His presence. This is an anthropomorphic phrase.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

▣ "He" Notice all the things that YHWH does for Cyrus II.

- arouses from the east

- calls in righteousness

- delivers up nations before him

- subdues kings

- like dust

- like chaff

Verse 3 describes the swiftness of his victories. Verse 4 describes
the Lord who accomplishes the victories for His own
purposes of redemption and restoration for His people.

NASB
"subdues"

NKJV
"rule over"

NRSV, JPSOA
"tramples"

TEV
"victory"

NJB
"subjects"

REB
"overthrowing"

Peshitta
"confounded"

The problem is the rare VERB (BDB 921, KB 1190, Hiphil
jussive). It basically means "have dominion over" or "rule" (NKJV). This
does not seem to fit the context, so the various options. The VERB must
refer to Cyrus.

verses.zh: 他追赶他们，走他所未走的道，坦然前行。
verses.en: He pursues them and passes by unharmed;[NOTE:1] he advances with great speed.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[in] peace”; KJV, ASV “safely”; NASB “in safety”; NIV “unscathed.”

Heb “a way with his feet he does not come [or “enter”].” One could translate, “by a way he was not [previously] entering with his feet.” This would mean that he is advancing into new territory and expanding his conquests. The present translation assumes this is a hyperbolic description of his speedy advance. He moves so quickly he does not enter the way with his feet, i.e., his feet don’t even touch the ground. See C. R. North, Second Isaiah, 94.
verses.commentary:
41:3

NASB
"traversing with his feet"

NKJV
"he had not gone with his feet"

NRSV, NJB
"scarcely touching the path with his feet"

REB
"swifter than any traveler on foot"

JPSOA
"no shackle is placed on his feet"

The Hebrew phrase is ambiguous. The ancient versions did not understand it.

- LXX ‒ "the way of his feet shall proceed in peace"

- Peshitta ‒ "he shall not pass that way on foot"

- DSS ‒ "they do not discern the path of his feet"

Most modern English translations see it as imagery of speed. However, the JPSOA (p. 864) translates
the word "path" (BDB 73) as "shackles" from an Old Aramaic root.

It could refer to new territory (NET Bible).

verses.zh: 谁行做成就这事，从起初宣召历代呢？就是我―耶和华！我是首先的，也与末后的同在。
verses.en: Who acts and carries out decrees?[NOTE:1] Who[NOTE:2] summons the successive generations from the beginning?I, the Lord, am present at the very beginning,and at the very end—I am the one.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Who acts and accomplishes?”; NASB “Who has performed and accomplished it.”
The interrogative particle is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
Heb “I, the Lord, [am with] the first, and with the last ones I [am] he.”
verses.commentary:
41:4 "Calling forth the generations from the beginning" This is an idiom for YHWH's control of time and
history (cf. Isa. 40:21; 41:26; 44:7; 45:21). YHWH directs creation, the call of Abraham, and his seed for
His purposes. OT predictive prophecy is the strongest evidentiary basis for the inspired Bible!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ For "beginning" see

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAD.

▣ "'I, the Lord, am the first, and with the last. I am He'" There
is a series of Hebraic terms and forms used here to describe God.

- "the Lord" comes from the Hebrew VERB
"to be" (cf. Exod. 3:14, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.)

- "the first and the last" (cf. Isa. 44:6; 48:12; Rev. 1:8; 21:6)

- "I am He" reflects the term "YHWH" (cf. Isa. 43:10; 44:4; John 8:24,28,57-58; 13:19; 18:5)

Collectively, these terms seem to reflect that God is the only-living, ever-living
God (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM). The imagery is used for Jesus, YHWH's Messiah, in
Rev. 1:17; 2:8; 22:13. (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH)

verses.zh: 海岛看见就都害怕；地极也都战兢，就近前来。
verses.en: The coastlands[NOTE:1] see and are afraid;the whole earth[NOTE:2] trembles;they approach and come.
notes: Or “islands” (NIV, CEV); NCV “faraway places”; NLT “lands beyond the sea.”
Heb “the ends of the earth,” but this is a merism, where the earth’s extremities stand for its entirety, i.e., the extremities and everything in between them.
verses.commentary:
41:5 "The ends of the earth" This second line is parallel to "the coastlands," see note at Isa. 41:1. They
both refer to the whole "known" Mediterranean and Near Eastern world.

verses.zh: 他们各人帮助邻舍，各人对弟兄说：壮胆吧！
verses.en: They help one another;[NOTE:1] one says to the other, ‘Be strong!’
notes: Heb “each his neighbor helps”; NCV “The workers help each other.”
verses.commentary:
41:6-7 The Hebrew VERB "make strong" (BDB 304, KB 302) is used three
times in these verses.

- Qal IMPERATIVE ‒ be strong, Isa. 41:6

- Piel IMPERFECT with waw ‒ encourage,
Isa. 41:7

- Piel IMPERFECT with waw ‒ fastens it,
Isa. 41:7

The nations looked to each other's deity for help, but in vain, for their gods could not see,
hear, or act! Oh, the tragedy of human superstition and imagination!

verses.zh: 木匠勉励银匠，用锤打光的勉励打砧的，论焊工说，焊得好；又用钉子钉稳，免得偶像动摇。
verses.en: The craftsman encourages the metalsmith,the one who wields the hammer encourages[NOTE:1] the one who pounds on the anvil.He approves the quality of the welding,[NOTE:2] and nails it down so it won’t fall over.
notes: The verb “encourages” is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
Heb “saying of the welding, ‘It is good.’”

verses.zh: 惟你以色列―我的仆人，雅各―我所拣选的，我朋友亚伯拉罕的后裔，
verses.en: “You, my servant Israel,Jacob, whom I have chosen,offspring of Abraham my friend,[NOTE:1]
notes: Or perhaps, “covenantal partner” (see 1 Kgs 5:15 HT [5:1 ET]; 2 Chr 20:7).
verses.commentary:
41:8 "But you, Israel, My servant" There has been much discussion over the term "My servant." It seems to
be used in three distinct ways in the OT.

- for an individual like the king or a prophet (cf. Num. 12:7)

- for the nation of Israel (cf. Isa. 42:19; 44:21)

- ultimately for the ideal Israelite, the Messiah (cf. Isa. 52:13-53:12)

In the book of Isaiah the second and third options are often merged.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

▣ "I have chosen" This VERB (BDB 103, KB 119, Qal
perfect) is an emphasis on God's election (cf. Isa. 41:9; 43:10; 44:1,2;
49:7; Deut. 7:6; 14:2). In the OT election was for service (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6), while
in the NT election is for salvation which leads to service.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

▣ "Descendant of Abraham My friend" Note YHWH's call and promise to Abraham in
Genesis 12; 15; 22. This foundational Patriarchal covenant is emphasized by Paul in Romans 4 and
Galatians 3. Abraham is also called YHWH's friend in 2 Chr. 20:7; James 2:23. They talked face to
face in Genesis 18.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

verses.zh: 你是我从地极所领（原文是抓）来的，从地角所召来的，且对你说：你是我的仆人；我拣选你，并不弃绝你。
verses.en: you whom I am bringing back[NOTE:1] from the earth’s extremitiesand have summoned from the remote regions—I told you, ‘You are my servant.’I have chosen you and not rejected you.
notes: Heb “whom I have taken hold of [i.e., to lead back].”
verses.commentary:
41:9 "You whom I have taken. . .called" Both VERBS are
PERFECTS (i.e. completed action).

- taken ‒ BDB 304, KB 302, Hiphil PERFECT

- called ‒ BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal PERFECT (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALLED)

Also note the synonymous parallelism between

- from the ends of the earth

- its remotest parts

In context this refers to the places that Assyria resettled (i.e. exiled) the Israelites
(722 B.C.) and Babylon resettled the Judeans (605, 597, 586,
582 B.C.).

▣ "I have chosen you and not rejected you" Judah felt that God had rejected them because
of the exile and destruction of Jerusalem and the temple by Nebuchadnezzar II in 586 B.C.
(i.e. 2 Sam. 7: 1 Chr. 17).

The VERB "reject" (BDB 549, KB 540, Qal
PERFECT, NEGATED) is used in Lev. 26:44, where YHWH promises not to
totally cut off His people because of their sin and covenant breaking. The question comes, how is
this promise affected by the NT? It seems to me there are two main options.

- Israel still has a crucial place in end-time events (i.e. Zech. 12:10;Romans 9-11).

- God's people have always been those who trust Him and live for Him. In the OT this referred to
the seed of Abraham, but also notice

- Melchizedek (Genesis 14)

- Job (Job 1)

- Jethro (Exodus)

- Caleb (Joshua)

- Uriah (2 Samuel 11)

- and others who were not Israelites

- In the NT this is widened to all believing Gentiles (i.e. Rom. 2:28-29; Galatians 3).

verses.zh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在；不要惊惶，因为我是你的　神。我必坚固你，我必帮助你；我必用我公义的右手扶持你。
verses.en: Don’t be afraid, for I am with you!Don’t be frightened, for I am your God![NOTE:1] I strengthen you—yes, I help you—yes, I uphold you with my victorious right hand![NOTE:2]
notes: According to BDB (1043 s.v. שָׁעָה), the verb תִּשְׁתָּע (tishtaʿ) in the second line of the poetic couplet is a Hitpael form from the root שָׁעָה (shaʿah, “gaze,” with metathesis of the stem prefix and the first root letter). Taking the Hitpael as iterative, one may then translate “do not anxiously look about.” However, the alleged Hitpael form of שָׁעָה (shaʿah) only occurs here and in verse 23. HALOT 1671 s.v. שׁתע proposes that the verb is instead a Qal form from the root שׁתע (“fear”). Its attestation in cognate Semitic languages, including Ugaritic (discovered after the publishing of BDB), suggests the existence of this root. The poetic structure of v. 10 also supports the proposal, for the form in question is in synonymous parallelism to יָרֵא (yareʾ, “fear”).

The “right hand” is a symbol of the Lord’s power to deliver (Exod 15:6, 12) and protect (Ps 63:9 HT [63:8 ET]). Here צֶדֶק (tsedeq) has its well-attested nuance of “vindicated righteousness,” i.e., “victory, deliverance” (see 45:8; 51:5, and BDB 841-42 s.v.).
verses.commentary:
41:10 "Do not fear" This is a very common message from YHWH to His people (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal
IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense, negated, cf. Isa. 41:13,14; 43:1,5; 44:2,8;
51:7,12; 54:4,14). See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR

Notice why they should not fear.

- YHWH is personally with them

- YHWH is their covenant God

- He will strengthen them

- He will help them (Isa. 41:10,14)

- He will uphold them (Isa. 41:10,13)

- all who oppose them will

- be shamed

- be dishonored

- be brought to nothing (Isa. 41:11-12)

- perish

▣ "for I am with you" There is no stated verb in this phrase (see NKJV).
There is an obvious intended word play (cf. Isa. 41:13) between the meaning of the needed
verb (I am) and the name for God, YHWH (I Am that I Am, cf. Exod. 3:14). There is no
greater promise in all the Bible (cf. Matt. 28:20; Acts 18:10). This truth is reflected in the Messianic title, "Emmanuel" (Isa. 7:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

NASB
"Do not anxiously look about you"

NKJV, Peshitta
"be not discourged"

NRSV, REB
"do not be afraid"

TEV
"let nothing terrify you"

NJB
"do not be alarmed"

LXX
"wander not"

JPSOA
"Be not frightened"

The Hebrew VERB (תשׁעה, BDB 1043,
KB 1609) in the Hithpael, means "gaze not about (in anxiety)."

It is possible that the VERB is from another root (שׁתע),
which is found in Ugaritic, meaning "fear" (NET Bible, p. 1250, #21), and therefore, a parallel with line 1.

▣

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, REB, JPSOA
"with My righteous right hand"

TEV
"I will protect you and save you"

NJB
"with my saving right hand"

Peshitta
"with the right hand of my righteousness"

LXX
"with my just right hand"

The translation question is MASCULINE NOUN (BDB 841), which is
the term usually translated "righteousness," but here, the connotation of "victorious" (BDB 842, #6. d., cf. Isa. 51:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

verses.zh: 凡向你发怒的必都抱愧蒙羞；与你相争的必如无有，并要灭亡。
verses.en: Look, all who were angry at you will be ashamed and humiliated;your adversaries[NOTE:1] will be reduced to nothing[NOTE:2] and perish.
notes: Heb “the men of your strife”; NASB “those who contend with you.”
Heb “like nothing”; NAB “come to nought.”
verses.commentary:
41:11 "all those. . .those who contend" Remember that YHWH has promised blessings to those who bless
His people and curses to those who curse them (cf. Gen. 12:3). It must be remembered that Israel's strength,
trust, and hope was in YHWH, not in themselves.

Notice how the returning Israelites' opponents are characterized.

- all those who are angered at you, Isa. 41:11

- those who contend with you, Isa. 41:11

- those who quarrel with you, Isa. 41:12

- those who war with you, Isa. 41:12

Also notice their fate.

- will be shamed, Isa. 41:11

- will be dishonored, Isa. 41:11

- will be as nothing, Isa. 41:11

- will perish, Isa. 41:11

- will not be found, Isa. 41:12

- will be as nothing, Isa. 41:12

- will be non-existent, Isa. 41:12

verses.zh: 与你争竞的，你要找他们也找不着；与你争战的必如无有，成为虚无。
verses.en: When you will look for your opponents,[NOTE:1] you will not find them;your enemies[NOTE:2] will be reduced to absolutely nothing.
notes: Heb “the men of your struggle”; NASB “those who quarrel with you.”
Heb “the men of your battle”; NAB “who do battle with you.”

verses.zh: 因为我耶和华―你的　神必搀扶你的右手，对你说：不要害怕！我必帮助你。
verses.en: For I am the Lord your God,the one who takes hold of your right hand,who says to you, ‘Don’t be afraid, I am helping you.’

verses.zh: 你这虫雅各和你们以色列人，不要害怕！耶和华说：我必帮助你。你的救赎主就是以色列的圣者。
verses.en: Don’t be afraid, despised, insignificant Jacob,[NOTE:1] men of[NOTE:2] Israel.I am helping you,” says the Lord,your Protector,[NOTE:3] the Holy One of Israel.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “O worm Jacob” (NAB, NIV84); NIV11 “you worm Jacob.” The worm metaphor suggests that Jacob is insignificant and despised.
On the basis of the parallelism (note “worm”) and an alleged Akkadian cognate, some read “louse” or “weevil.” Cf. NAB “O maggot Israel”; NRSV “you insect Israel.”
Heb “your kinsman redeemer.” A גֹּאֵל (goʾel, “kinsman redeemer”) was a protector of the extended family’s interests.
See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.
verses.commentary:
41:14 "you worm Jacob" This reference to Jacob as being a worm is not a derogatory
term, but seems to be imagery for his helplessness (cf. Job 25:6; Ps. 22:6) without God's aid, similar
to the imagery of Ezek. 16:6.

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA
"men"

NRSV
"insect"

NJB
"little handful"

REB, JPSOA footnote
"maggot"

NET footnote
"louse" or "weevil"

The MT has "men" (BDB 607) but modern translations emend it to
an Akkadian root (NRSV, REB, NET Bible, p. 1250, #28).

▣ "your Redeemer" This (Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPIAL title, cf. Isa. 43:14;
44:6,24; 49:7; 59:20) reflects
the Hebrew term Go'el (BDB 145, KB 169). This Hebrew term referred to the "kinsmen redeemer"
or "avenger." It is used of one who buys a near relative back from slavery or a prisoner of war (cf.
an example would be Boaz in Ruth 4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINSMAN REDEEMER

▣ "the Holy One of Israel" This is a favorite title for Israel's Deity in Isaiah (i.e. Assyrian period,
cf. Isa. 1:4; 5:19; 10:17,20; 12:6; 17:7; 29:19,23; 30:11,12,15; 31:1; 37:23; also in the second part of Isaiah in the
Neo-Babylonian period, Isa. 40:25; 41:14,16,20; 43:3,14, 15; 45:11; 47:4; 48:17; 49:7; 54:5; 55:5; 60:9,14). Because
He is "holy," His people should be holy (cf. Lev. 19:2; Matt. 5:48; 1 Pet. 1:16).

This title, in a sense, expresses the impossible tension of a sinful, fallen people conforming
to a holy standard. The Mosaic Covenant was impossible to keep (cf. Acts 15; Galatians 3; Hebrews). The old
covenant was a way to show the impossibility of humans to conform to God's standard, yet He was with them,
for them, preparing them for His answer to their fallen condition. He does not lower His standard, but provides
it through His Messiah. The new covenant (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36) is a covenant of faith and
repentance, not human performance (cf. Eph. 2:8-9), though it issues in Christlikeness (cf. James 2:14-26). God wants a people
who reflect His character to the nations (cf. Matt. 5:48).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SUPERIORITY OF THE NEW COVENANT OVER THE MOSAIC COVENANT

verses.zh: 看哪，我已使你成为有快齿打粮的新器具；你要把山岭打得粉碎，使冈陵如同糠秕。
verses.en: “Look, I am making you like[NOTE:1] a sharp threshing sledge,new and double-edged.[NOTE:2] You will thresh the mountains and crush them;you will make the hills like straw.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “into” (so NIV); ASV “have made thee to be.”
Heb “owner of two-mouths,” i.e., double-edged.
The mountains and hills symbolize hostile nations that are obstacles to Israel’s restoration.
verses.commentary:
41:15-16 Israel's enemies are described as "mountains" (BDB 249) and "hills" (BDB 148) which will be
"threshed," which is an agricultural term for harvesting by means of a heavy sledge (cf. Micah 4:13; Hab. 3:12). This is
Hebrew poetry, be careful of literalism!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY

verses.zh: 你要把它簸扬，风要吹去；旋风要把它刮散。你倒要以耶和华为喜乐，以以色列的圣者为夸耀。
verses.en: You will winnow them and the wind will blow them away;the wind will scatter them.You will rejoice in the Lord;you will boast in the Holy One of Israel.

verses.zh: 困苦穷乏人寻求水却没有；他们因口渴，舌头干燥。我―耶和华必应允他们；我―以色列的　神必不离弃他们。
verses.en: The oppressed and the poor look for water, but there is none;their tongues are parched from thirst.I, the Lord, will respond to their prayers;[NOTE:1] I, the God of Israel, will not abandon them.
notes: Heb “will answer them” (so ASV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).
verses.commentary:
41:17-20 These verses reflect God's presence and blessing with the Judean returnees with
imagery from abundance in nature (cf. Lev. 26; Deut. 27; 28). This abundance was meant to attract the nations to YHWH.

As YHWH provided food, water, and protection (i.e. His presence with Israel during the
Exodus), He will do it again. In a sense, this was a second exodus of Israel from foreign bondage.

For a good list of future prosperity promises, see Isa. 32:20. Prosperity was linked to

- covenant obedience (Lev. 26; Deut. 28)

- restoration of the covenant people to Canaan

- a way to attract the nations to YHWH

verses.zh: 我要在净光的高处开江河，在谷中开泉源；我要使沙漠变为水池，使干地变为涌泉。
verses.en: I will make streams flow down the slopesand produce springs in the middle of the valleys.I will turn the wilderness into a pool of waterand the arid land into springs.

verses.zh: 我要在旷野种上香柏树、皂荚树、番石榴树，和野橄榄树。我在沙漠要把松树、杉树，并黄杨树一同栽植；
verses.en: I will make cedars, acacias, myrtles, and olive trees grow in the wilderness;I will make evergreens, firs, and cypresses grow together in the arid rift valley.[NOTE:1]
notes: The rift valley (עֲרָבָה, ʿaravah) is known for its arid, desert-like conditions in the area of the Dead Sea and southward (although it also includes the Jordan Valley, extending from Galilee to the Gulf of Aqaba). The point here is the contrast from its normal arid conditions to being productive with trees, which implies being watered. Similarly, the wilderness (מִדְבָּר, midbar) in the first line is an area that receives less than twelve inches of rainfall annually and so cannot support trees.
verses.commentary:
41:19 For a good resource for identifying ancient plants and animals see UBS Fauna and Flora of
the Bible.

verses.zh: 好叫人看见、知道、思想、明白；这是耶和华的手所做的，是以色列的圣者所造的。
verses.en: I will do this so[NOTE:1] people[NOTE:2] will observe and recognize,so they will pay attention and understandthat the Lord’s power[NOTE:3] has accomplished this,and that the Holy One of Israel has brought it into being.[NOTE:4]
notes: The words “I will do this” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The Hebrew text has here simply, “in order that.”
Heb “they”; NAB, NRSV “that all may see”; CEV, NLT “Everyone will see.”
Heb “hand” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV).
Or “created it” (KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV); TEV “has made it happen.”

verses.zh: 耶和华对假神说：你们要呈上你们的案件；雅各的君说：你们要声明你们确实的理由。
verses.en: “Present your argument,” says the Lord.“Produce your evidence,”[NOTE:1] says Jacob’s King.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “strong [words],” see HALOT 870 s.v. *עֲצֻמוֹת.
Apparently this challenge is addressed to the pagan idol gods, see vv. 23-24.
verses.commentary:
41:21 This is a court scene (cf. Isa. 41:1). This same type of imagery is found in Isa. 1:18-20).

▣ "The King of Jacob says" This title occurs only here. YHWH was the ideal King of the Covenant
people (cf. Isa. 43:15; 44:6; Exod. 15:18; Num. 23:21; Jdg. 8:23; 1 Sam. 8:7; 12:12; 1 Kgs. 22:19; Isa. 6:5). Jacob's
name (i.e. Israel) represents all the Covenant people, all thirteen tribes (cf. Isa. 45:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

verses.zh: 可以声明，指示我们将来必遇的事，说明先前的是甚么事，好叫我们思索，得知事的结局，或者把将来的事指示我们。
verses.en: “Let them produce evidence! Let them tell us what will happen!Tell us about your earlier predictive oracles,[NOTE:1] so we may examine them[NOTE:2] and see how they were fulfilled.[NOTE:3] Or decree for us some future events!
notes: Heb “As for the former things, tell us what they are!”
Heb “so we might set [them to] our heart.”
Heb “and might know their outcome.”
verses.commentary:
41:22-23 Predictive prophecy is one of the strongest evidences of the inspiration of the Bible.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

41:22-24 This refers to the national gods. God calls on them to act or predict or do anything, but they
cannot because they are vanity or nothingness (Isa. 41:24,28-29).

verses.zh: 要说明后来的事，好叫我们知道你们是　神。你们或降福，或降祸，使我们惊奇，一同观看。
verses.en: Predict how future events will turn out,[NOTE:1] so we might know you are gods.Yes, do something good or something bad, so we might be frightened and in awe.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Declare the coming things, with respect to the end.”

The translation assumes the Qere (וְנִרְאֶה [venirʾeh], from יָרֵא [yareʾ], “be afraid”).tn Heb “so we might be frightened and afraid together.” On the meaning of the verb שָׁתָע (shataʿ), see the note at v. 10.
verses.commentary:
41:23 This verse is one of the places where the compilers of the MT recognized a Hebrew variant
and suggested a change. The MT is not the oldest Hebrew MSS. It was not completed until A.D.
900 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MASORETIC TEXT)

The MT has "and we shall see," 23c (Qere, ונראה,
BDB 906, Qal IMPERFECT, NKJV, Leupold), but they suggest "and we shall be afraid"
(ketiv, ונרא, BDB 431, Qal IMPERFECT,
NASB). The UBS Text Project, p. 104, gives "see" a B rating (some doubt).

41:24b

NASB
"amounts to nothing"

NKJV
"is nothing"

NRSV
"is nothing at all"

NJB
"less than nothing"

REB
"none existant"

JPSOA
"less than nullify"

Peshitta
"corrupt"

The NOUN (BDB 67, KB 79) is found only here. Most
translations take it as parallel to "nothing" (BDB 34 II) in line one.

KB Lexicon gives several guesses

- something worthless

- chaotic

- void

- illusion

The UBS Text Project, p. 104, lists two possible Hebrew roots.

- מאפע (BDB 67)

It gives option #1 only a "C" rating (considerable doubt). Please remember, even
though we are not sure of the meaning of a word

- the larger context

still provide the inspired message!

verses.zh: 看哪，你们属乎虚无；你们的作为也属乎虚空。那选择你们的是可憎恶的。
verses.en: Look, you are nothing, and your accomplishments are nonexistent;the one who chooses to worship you is disgusting.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “an object of disgust [is he who] chooses you.”

verses.zh: 我从北方兴起一人；他是求告我名的，从日出之地而来。他必临到掌权的，好像临到灰泥，彷佛窑匠踹泥一样。
verses.en: I have stirred up one out of the north[NOTE:1] and he advances,one from the eastern horizon who prays in my name.[NOTE:2] He steps on[NOTE:3] rulers as if they were clay,like a potter treading the clay.
notes: That is, Cyrus the Persian. See the note at v. 2.
Heb “[one] from the rising of the sun [who] calls in my name.”
The Hebrew text has וְיָבֹא (veyavoʾ, “and he comes”), but this likely needs to be emended to an original וַיָּבָס (vayyavas), from בּוּס (bus, “step on”).
verses.commentary:
41:25 "have aroused one from the north" This again refers to Cyrus II (cf. Isa. 41:2; 44:28; 45:1). The
only direction that one could come into Palestine from the Fertile Crescent was from the north because a
desert was directly to the east (i.e. "from the rising of the sun").

▣ "he will call on My name" This may refer to Cyrus' proclamation recorded in 2 Chr. 36:22-23 and Ezra 1:1-2.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

NASB
"he will come upon rulers"

NKJV
"he will come against princes"

NRSV, TEV, NJB
"he shall trample on rulers"

REB
"he marches over rulers"

JPSOA
"he has trampled rulers"

NET
"he steps on rulers"

The MT has the common VERB "come" (בוא, BDB 97,
KB 112, Qal IMPERFECT) which several translations assume from context,
means "step on." The UBS Textual Project, p. 106, suggests another possible root.

- ויבא ‒ he will come (MT)

- ויבס ‒ he will tread upon

However, the UBS Text Project put #1 in the text but gave it a "C" rating (considerable doubt).
The NET Bible likes option #2 (p. 1251 #18).

verses.zh: 谁从起初指明这事，使我们知道呢？谁从先前说明，使我们说他不错呢？谁也没有指明；谁也没有说明；谁也没有听见你们的话。
verses.en: Who decreed this from the beginning, so we could know?Who announced it[NOTE:1] ahead of time, so we could say, ‘He’s correct’?Indeed, none of them decreed it.Indeed, none of them announced it.Indeed, no one heard you say anything!
notes: The words “who announced it” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The interrogative particle and verb are understood by ellipsis (see the preceding line).
verses.commentary:
41:26 YHWH shows His existence and power by His prophesied acts in history (cf. Isa. 43:9; 45:21). This
may refer to Isa. 30:8, where YHWH tells the prophet to write down His prophecy so that the accuracy of His
predictions prove His power, knowledge, and control over human history.

verses.zh: 我首先对锡安说：看哪，我要将一位报好信息的赐给耶路撒冷。
verses.en: I first decreed to Zion, ‘Look, here’s what will happen!’[NOTE:1] I sent a herald to Jerusalem.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew text reads simply, “First to Zion, ‘Look here they are!’” The words “I decreed” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
41:27 "here they are" This seems to refer to true prophets, as Isa. 41:28 and 29 refer to false
prophets and the tragedy of people turning to helpless idols.

verses.zh: 我看的时候并没有人；我问的时候，他们中间也没有谋士可以回答一句。
verses.en: I look, but there is no one,among them there is no one who serves as an adviserthat I might ask questions and receive answers.

verses.zh: 看哪，他们和他们的工作都是虚空，且是虚无。他们所铸的偶像都是风，都是虚的。
verses.en: Look, all of them are nothing,[NOTE:1] their accomplishments are nonexistent;their metal images lack any real substance.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew text has אָוֶן (ʾaven, “deception,” i.e., “false”), but the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has אין (“nothing”), which forms a better parallel with אֶפֶס (ʾefes, “nothing”) in the next line. See also 40:17 and 41:12.
Heb “their statues are wind and nothing”; NASB “wind and emptiness”; NIV “wind and confusion.”
verses.commentary:
41:29 Isaiah describes the pagan national gods/idols (i.e. molten images, BDB 651) in four words.

- a delusion (BDB 19)

- nothing (BDB 67)

- their works are wind (BDB 924)

- empty (BDB 1062)

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- In this chapter YHWH displays His power and sovereignty by calling Cyrus II (i.e. the to be king of Persia,
cf. Isa. 41:2,25) to take over the rule of the Fertile Crescent from Neo-Babylon. This regime change will show

- YHWH's plan of deliverance for His people (i.e. return from exile)

- YHWH's judgment of the idols of the peoples who cannot hear, see, or act

- Chapter 41 has an extensive number of commands used as a rhetorical literary device.

- directed to the "coastlands," Isa. 41:1

- "listen to Me" ‒ BDB 361, KB 357, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- "let the peoples gain new strength" ‒ BDB 322, KB 321, Hiphil IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

- "let them come forward" ‒ BDB 620, KB 670, Qal IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense

- "let them speak" ‒ BDB 180, KB 210, Piel IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense

- "let us come together for judgment" ‒ BDB 897, KB 1132, Qal COHORTATIVE

- directed to "one from the east" (i.e. Cyrus II), Isa. 41:2 ‒ BDB 921, KB 1190, Hiphil JUSSIVE (i.e. Persia)

- the coastlands speak to each other, "be strong" Isa. 41:6 ‒ BDB 304, KB 302, Qal IMPERATIVE

- YHWH speaks to His people

- "do not fear" Isa. 41:10 ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT used
in a JUSSIVE sense (also note Isa. 41:13, 14; see SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR)

- "do not anxiously look about you" Isa. 41:10 ‒ BDB 1043, KB 1609, Hithpael JUSSIVE

- YHWH (and the heavenly council; see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS)
as Judge calls the idols to court (Isa. 41:21-24)

- "present your cases" ‒ BDB 897, KB 1132, Piel IMPERATIVE

- "bring forward your strong arguments" ‒ BDB 620, KB 670, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- "let them bring forth" ‒ BDB 620, KB 670, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- "let them declare to us" ‒ BDB 616, KB 665, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- "as for the former events, declare what they were" ‒ BDB 616, KB 665, Hiphil
IMPERATIVE

- "that we may consider them" ‒ BDB 962, KB 1321, Qal COHORTATIVE

- "that we may know their outcome" ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Qal COHORTATIVE

- "announce to us what is coming" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- "declare the things that are going to come forward" ‒ BDB 616, KB 665, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- "that we may know that you are gods" ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Qal COHORTATIVE

- "do good" ‒ BDB 405, KB 408, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- "do evil" ‒ BDB 949, KB 1269, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- "that we may anxiously look about us" ‒ BDB 1043, KB 1609, Hithpael COHORTATIVE

- "and fear together" ‒ BDB 431, KB 432 (or BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal COHORTATIVE), Qal
JUSSIVE

- YHWH gives His verdict on the idols in Isa. 41:25-29

- "who has declared this" ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Qal COHORTATIVE

- "that we may say, 'he is right'?" ‒ BDB 55, KB 65, Qal IMPERFECT, but in a COHORTATIVE sense

- "when I look, there is no one" ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal JUSSIVE

- There is a symbolic trial where the nations are called to account (Isa. 41:1,21) because instead
of repentance in the face of YHWH's presence, power and prediction, they make new idols.

- Notice the number of times "I" is used. YHWH chooses to act. This is similar to Ezek. 36:27-36.

- The new exodus from exile is described in agricultural terms as it was in Isaiah 35. The promises
of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-29 are now realized.

- Israel has been restored to covenant status by YHWH's mercy and power.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 41:1-4

1"Coastlands, listen to Me in silence,

And let the peoples gain new strength;

Let them come forward, then let them speak;

Let us come together for judgment.

2Who has aroused one from the east

Whom He calls in righteousness to His feet?

He delivers up nations before him

And subdues kings.

He makes them like dust with his sword,

As the wind-driven chaff with his bow.

3He pursues them, passing on in safety,

By a way he had not been traversing with his feet.

4Who has performed and accomplished it,

Calling forth the generations from the beginning?

'I, the Lord, am the first, and with the last. I am He.'"
